cues.en: was given to me by one of the operational people that I, interviewed was stuff don't work as advertised,
cues.zh: 是我采访的一位运维人员告诉我的，叫做“东西不像广告里说的那样运作”，

cues.en: which is a real problem because there's lots of stuff that we have in our systems that we don't actually try out for many many years after they're installed and then we go out and try and use it and find out that it doesn't work the way that we expected.
cues.zh: 这真是个大问题，因为我们系统里的很多东西，在安装后的很多年里我们根本不会去试用，然后等我们跑去用的时候，才发现它根本不是我们期望的那样工作。

cues.en: That novel conditions are common,
cues.zh: 新情况很常见，

cues.en: that things that you haven't seen before actually do occur relatively frequently.
cues.zh: 没见过的事情其实会相对频繁地发生。

cues.en: That there's lots of adapting and tailoring, that is systems are not
cues.zh: 有大量适配和定制，也就是说系统并不是

cues.en: sort of working out of the box, they
cues.zh: 能开箱即用的，它们

cues.en: but if they did they don't work out of the box, they have to be tweaked and tuned and coddled and
cues.zh: 但即便能，它们也不是开箱即用的，得被微调、调优、哄着、

cues.en: stroked and kissed and prayed to and you have to burn the right kind of incense in order to get your systems to run.
cues.zh: 抚摸着、亲吻着、祈祷着，还得烧对香，系统才能跑起来。

cues.en: There's a lot of tailoring that goes on where people twist and turn and shave
cues.zh: 有很多定制在发生：人们会拧来拧去、转来转去、削掉

cues.en: off here and turn on and turn off various kinds of services and start and stop other kinds of things and set parameters to try and make the thing go, I call that tailoring.
cues.zh: 这里一点，打开或关闭各种服务，启动和停止其他东西，设置参数，试图让这东西跑起来，我把这叫定制。

cues.en: You tailor the systems that you work with. And then there's the unanticipated variety that comes along, people start using your system in ways that you didn't expect them to, they're using it for things that
cues.zh: 你会定制自己使用的系统。然后还有随之而来的意外多样性：人们开始以你没想到的方式使用你的系统，拿它来做一些

cues.en: you didn't plan them to use it for, for instance starting to use
cues.zh: 你没计划让他们用来做的事，比如开始用

cues.en: your email system for something like sending great large files around or things like that.
cues.zh: 你的邮件系统来发送超大文件之类的东西。

cues.en: And against all this, there's this continuous change of technology and people. There's constant
cues.zh: 而面对这一切，还有技术和人的持续变化。不断有

cues.en: moving of things going around all the time so that the world that you live in is anything but static.
cues.zh: 事物一直在流动变化，所以你身处的世界绝不是静态的。

cues.en: And finally, what's common with all these worlds, they're coping all the time with both shallow and deep conflicts. Shallow conflicts, can we make a little more, can this run a little better, am I getting along with this person, is this guy giving me a hard time on the phone, and deep conflicts like we really have to trade off something here, are we going to take the system down for a while to try and fix this, or are we going to try and fix it on the fly? The kind of decision that you have to make all the time.
cues.zh: 最后，这些世界的共同点是，它们一直要应对浅层和深层冲突。浅层冲突，能不能多做出一点，能不能跑得更好一点，我和这个人合得来吗，电话里这家伙是不是在为难我；深层冲突，比如这里真的得做取舍，是要把系统停一段时间来修，还是试着在线修？就是你得一直做的那种决定。

cues.en: If you sum all this stuff up, it's really summed up in sort of two phrases. The first is that the normal world is not well behaved.
cues.zh: 把这些都总结起来，其实就两句话。第一句是，正常世界并不守规矩。

cues.en: Those of you who feel like you live in a well behaved, well structured, very predictable, nice world are probably living in a fantasy or you're not operational people.
cues.zh: 如果你们有人觉得自己生活在一个守规矩、结构良好、高度可预测的美好世界里，那多半是活在幻想里，或者你不是做运维的人。

cues.en: In fact, if there's anybody in here who does feel that way,
cues.zh: 事实上，如果这里真有人这么觉得，

cues.en: we would like to know what company you work for because we're all going to sell the stock that we own in that company.
cues.zh: 我们倒想知道你在哪家公司上班，因为我们大家都会去卖掉手里那家公司的股票。

cues.en: The other thing is that's so interesting is that
cues.zh: 另一件很有意思的事是，

cues.en: even so, even though the world is so badly behaved,
cues.zh: 即便如此，尽管世界如此不守规矩，

cues.en: in a lot of operational settings we have a lot of success.
cues.zh: 在很多运维场景里，我们还是取得了不少成功。

cues.en: And the real question that we're faced with is, is this because of or in spite of
cues.zh: 而我们真正面对的问题是，这究竟是因为

cues.en: the designs of the systems that we have?
cues.zh: 我们系统的设计，还是 despite 这些设计？

cues.en: Are we getting the successes that we have because they're designed into the system or are coming from some other source? And that brings me to this idea about systems as imagined versus systems as found and I think this is a pretty big divide and it's an important one to get a hold of.
cues.zh: 我们的成功是因为系统设计得好，还是来自别的什么来源？这就引出了我想说的：想象中的系统 vs 实际发现的系统，我觉得这是个大分野，很重要，得抓住。

cues.en: Most systems are imagined, they do not, very very few people have much contact with the system as found. Systems are imagined,
cues.zh: 大多数系统都是想象中的，很少有人真正接触到实际发现的系统。系统是想象出来的，

cues.en: their state diagrams
cues.zh: 它们的状态图

cues.en: and their layouts of rack panels and their floor diagrams and all sorts of this, these are systems as imagined. It's the way we make stuff and they're static and deterministic.
cues.zh: 机架面板布局、机房平面图等等，这些都是想象中的系统。这是我们造东西的方式，它们是静态的、确定性的。

cues.en: Those
cues.zh: Those

cues.en: systems as imagined have static and deterministic kinds of qualities.
cues.zh: 想象中的系统具有静态和确定性的特质。

cues.en: Systems as found look more like this.
cues.zh: 而实际发现的系统看起来更像这样。

cues.en: You recognize the use of an antiquated device for communication
cues.zh: 你能认出这是在用一台过时的通信设备

cues.en: with a long coiled wire on it and the positioning of the person suggesting that the communication is taking place under some sort of stress.
cues.zh: 上面拖着一根长长的盘绕电线，人物的姿势表明通信是在某种压力下进行的。

cues.en: Here's another nice photograph.
cues.zh: 这是另一张不错的照片。

cues.en: Some of you will recognize this as your own system.
cues.zh: 你们中有些人会认出这是你们自己的系统。

cues.en: If you cannot read the sign there it do
cues.zh: 如果你看不清那里的标牌，上面写的是

cues.en: not touch any of these wires.
cues.zh: 不要触碰这些电线中的任何一根。

cues.en: And what you rarely see in systems
cues.zh: 而在系统中你很少见到的

cues.en: as imagined
cues.zh: 在想象中的系统里

cues.en: is this sort of picture, people actually doing work, people sitting in front of screens making the system run.
cues.zh: 就是这种画面：人们实际在干活，人们坐在屏幕前让系统运转起来。

cues.en: And these systems, the systems that has found,
cues.zh: 而这些系统，即实际发现的系统，

cues.en: are dynamic and stochastic.
cues.zh: 是动态且随机的。

cues.en: They are not deterministic,
cues.zh: 它们不是确定性的，

cues.en: they are entirely stochastic.
cues.zh: 它们完全是随机的。

cues.en: Their performance cannot be deterministically,
cues.zh: 它们的性能无法被确定性地

cues.en: defined. It is a stochastic process.
cues.zh: 定义。它是一个随机过程。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: to make things worse, as one of the people in this room said,
cues.zh: 更糟的是，正如这个房间里有人说过的那样，

cues.en: we're always doing some sort of maintenance.
cues.zh: 我们总是在做某种维护。

cues.en: The maintenance intervals is essentially zero.
cues.zh: 维护间隔基本上为零。

cues.en: The MTBB,
cues.zh: MTBB，

cues.en: the mean time between,
cues.zh: 即平均间隔时间，

cues.en: MTBM,
cues.zh: MTBM，

cues.en: the mean time between maintenance is zero.
cues.zh: 即平均维护间隔时间为零。

cues.en: You're always doing something.
cues.zh: 你总是在做些什么。

cues.en: So if we compare these two views now, you've got the as imagined view represented by the state diagram, this is a static view, it's a deterministic type system,
cues.zh: 所以现在如果我们比较这两种视角，你有由状态图表示的想象视角，这是一个静态视角，是一个确定性类型的系统，

cues.en: it's encountered during design, it's encountered during development, it's the only way you can develop these systems,
cues.zh: 它在设计阶段遇到，在开发阶段遇到，这是你开发这些系统的唯一方式，

cues.en: and it's encountered in reviews of outcomes
cues.zh: 并且在结果评审中遇到，

cues.en: after systems have failed. Any kind of review or evaluation of a system after failure is always done in this as imagined kind of world.
cues.zh: 在系统失败之后。系统失败后的任何形式的评审或评估，总是在这种想象的世界中进行的。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: sort of archetype of this is
cues.zh: 这算是某种原型吧

cues.en: a state transition diagram or for failures it would be something like
cues.zh: 状态转移 diagram 或者针对失败它可能是类似这样的something like

cues.en: a fault tree analysis. Some of you probably do fault trees, some of you may do
cues.zh: 故障树分析。你们中有些人可能做故障树，有些人可能做

cues.en: probabilistic risk assessments. But that's basically a system as imagined. The system is found,
cues.zh: 概率风险评估。但那基本上是一个想象中的系统。系统被发现时，

cues.en: is characterized by being dynamic, it's constantly changing, it's stochastic, it's predictable
cues.zh: 它的特征是动态性，它在不断变化，它是随机的，它是可预测的

cues.en: in some sort of statistical way.
cues.zh: 以某种统计方式。

cues.en: And it's what we encounter during implementation,
cues.zh: 这也是我们在实现过程中会遇到的，

cues.en: during operations, and during maintenance and recovery from transients.
cues.zh: 在运行期间，以及在进行维护和从瞬态故障中恢复期间。

cues.en: And it's
cues.zh: 而且它是

cues.en: really hard to draw these things. One of the ways to do it is with a FRAM drawing.
cues.zh: 把这些画出来真的很不容易。其中一种办法是用 FRAM 图来画。

cues.en: FRAM is a functional resonance analysis method developed by a friend of mine named Eric Holnaggle.
cues.zh: FRAM 是一种功能共振分析方法，由我的朋友 Eric Holnaggle 开发。

cues.en: When we look at these systems as found though, we ask the questions broadly, and I mean this not just for your groups but across all of these different groups that we've studied,
cues.zh: 当我们把这些系统当作已有系统来看时，我们会宽泛地提出问题，我的意思不只是你们的小组，而是我们研究过的所有这些不同小组，

cues.en: What are people doing in these as found systems? What does operations look like? And it's really got four components. It's got some monitoring activity, that is people looking at the system to try and understand what's going on in it. It's got some responding activity, that is responding
cues.zh: 在这些已发现的系统里，人们都在做什么？运维是什么样子的？它其实包含四个组成部分。其中有监控活动，也就是人们观察系统，试图理解系统内部发生了什么。还有响应活动，也就是做出响应

cues.en: not in a reacting sort of sense, but responding in the sense of understanding what's happening in the system and trying to anticipate where it's going and make changes
cues.zh: 不是反应式的，而是响应式的——理解系统中正在发生什么，尝试预判它的走向并做出改变

cues.en: to deal with that. They are constantly adapting,
cues.zh: 应对这个问题。他们一直在适应，

cues.en: that is they are trying to make the system work differently
cues.zh: 也就是说，他们正试图让系统以不同的方式运行

cues.en: so that they can get it to behave in a better way.
cues.zh: 这样他们就能让它的表现更好。

cues.en: And significantly
cues.zh: 而且重要的是

cues.en: there's a lot of learning going on about the system. The system, the learning in the system is a key component of what's happening and that learning is taking place in operational communities that most of us don't ever have any contact with.
cues.zh: 关于系统有大量学习在进行。系统内的学习是正在发生的事情的关键组成部分，而这种学习发生在运维社区里，我们大多数人从未接触过这些社区。

cues.en: There are groups of operators,
cues.zh: 有一些操作员群体，

cues.en: there are groups of people who very often are doing shift work, very often paid by the hour,
cues.zh: 有些群体经常做轮班工作，常常按小时计酬，

cues.en: very often anonymous in corporate hierarchies,
cues.zh: 常常在公司层级中不具名，

cues.en: very often people who are
cues.zh: 常常是那些

cues.en: largely outside of the social groups that most of you tend to travel in.
cues.zh: 很大程度上处在你们大多数人通常交往的社交群体之外的人。

cues.en: But they are the sources of what we call now resilience.
cues.zh: 但他们正是我们现在所称韧性的来源。

cues.en: Resilience is the combination
cues.zh: 韧性是这种组合

cues.en: in systems of these four kinds of activities,
cues.zh: 在系统中由这四类活动组成，

cues.en: these qualities
cues.zh: 这些品质

cues.en: are the qualities that go together to form resilience.
cues.zh: 共同构成了韧性。

cues.en: If you looked at this again and you thought about it, what are we talking about here? We're talking about monitoring and responding and adapting and learning and we're actually putting those all together,
cues.zh: 如果你再看一遍并想一想，我们到底在谈什么？我们在谈监控、响应、适应和学习，并且实际上把它们全都放在一起，

cues.en: those are terms that are trying to describe what we mean by resilience.
cues.zh: 这些术语试图描述我们所说的韧性。

cues.en: And in
cues.zh: 而且，在

cues.en: fact, the question is what are we doing? Well,
cues.zh: 事实上，问题是我们到底在做什么？嗯，

cues.en: when we design these systems, we design them for reliability,
cues.zh: 当我们设计这些系统时，是为可靠性而设计，

cues.en: that's the code word that you encounter most of the time, how reliable
cues.zh: 这就是你最常遇到的关键词：有多可靠

cues.en: is the system in which you're working. And what does reliability involve? It involves
cues.zh: 你工作的系统有多可靠？可靠性包括什么？它包括

cues.en: making stiff boundaries,
cues.zh: 设置刚性边界，

cues.en: lots of layers, lots of formalisms,
cues.zh: 大量层级、大量形式化方法，

cues.en: lots of defense in-depth,
cues.zh: 大量纵深防御，

cues.en: lots of redundancies,
cues.zh: 大量冗余，

cues.en: lots of interference protection,
cues.zh: 大量干扰防护，

cues.en: various kinds of securities around your systems,
cues.zh: 系统周围的各种安全机制，

cues.en: lots of things like abstractions
cues.zh: 大量抽象之类的东西

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: hiding of the details and various kinds of objects,
cues.zh: 隐藏细节和各种对象，

cues.en: lots of assurance mechanisms,
cues.zh: 大量保障机制，

cues.en: lots of formal reviews, and lots of accountability functions. That's what reliability
cues.zh: 大量正式评审，以及大量问责职能。这就是可靠性

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: made out of, and when you make reliability out of that stuff you do it at the design time. But what we really want in our systems is resilience.
cues.zh: 由这些东西构成的，而当你用这些东西构建可靠性时，你是在设计时完成的。但我们在系统中真正想要的是韧性。

cues.en: We want systems to be able to withstand transients, we want them to recover smoothly and swiftly from failures,
cues.zh: 我们希望系统能承受瞬态变化，也希望它们能从故障中平稳而迅速地恢复，

cues.en: we
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: want to be able to prioritize high level goals when the system's changing and we can't have to sacrifice something, we need to be able to choose which goals we should satisfy and which ones we should sacrifice.
cues.zh: 希望能在系统变化、不得不有所牺牲时，优先考虑高层目标；我们需要能选择满足哪些目标、牺牲哪些目标。

cues.en: We have to be able to recognize and respond to abnormal situations including situations that were never considered at design time.
cues.zh: 我们必须能够识别并响应异常情况，包括设计时从未考虑过的情况。

cues.en: And finally we have to find a way
cues.zh: 最后，我们必须找到一种方法

cues.en: to adapt to change. We have to find some way
cues.zh: 来适应变化。我们必须找到某种方法

cues.en: to make these systems which were designed
cues.zh: 让这些按

cues.en: in the mindset of four to seven years ago,
cues.zh: 四到七年前的理念设计出来的系统

cues.en: work for the next three to five years while we're building the systems that will be obsolete when we install them.
cues.zh: 在未来三到五年里继续工作，而我们正在构建的系统，等到安装时就已经过时了。

cues.en: So how do you design for resilience? We have this problem, we have the as imagined world that sits out there
cues.zh: 那么，如何为韧性而设计？我们面临这个问题：我们有一个想象中的世界，它就在那里

cues.en: and we have the as found world and there are two, as I've tried to suggest to you, two quite separate worlds.
cues.zh: 而我们有一个实际发现的世界；正如我试图向你们说明的，这是两个相当分离的世界。

cues.en: They look at different things, they work on different sorts of principles and the question is, can you bring them together? Can you get an as engineered
cues.zh: 它们关注不同的东西，遵循不同种类的原则；问题是，你能把它们结合起来吗？你能得到一个工程化的

cues.en: world that includes this quality of resilience?
cues.zh: 、包含这种韧性品质的世界吗？

cues.en: And this is not the $64,000
cues.zh: 而这不是那个 64,000 美元

cues.en: question,
cues.zh: 的问题，

cues.en: question, or maybe even more.
cues.zh: 的问题，甚至可能更多。

cues.en: In the world in which I normally work, it's the life and death question.
cues.zh: 在我通常工作的世界里，这是生死攸关的问题。

cues.en: But in the world in which you work, it may be the corporate life or death question.
cues.zh: 但在你们工作的世界里，这可能是企业的生死存亡问题。

cues.en: Can you make systems, can you actually engineer them ahead of time
cues.zh: 你能构建系统吗？你能提前对它们进行工程设计吗？

cues.en: so that it is possible in operational time
cues.zh: 从而使其在运行阶段

cues.en: for them to have the resilience that you want them to have.
cues.zh: 具备你所期望的韧性。

cues.en: And I would say to you that I think that this is true and I'm going to try and give you a list of things that I think you could do in designing your systems
cues.zh: 我想告诉你，我认为这是可行的，我尝试为你列举一些在设计系统时可以采取的做法

cues.en: that would lead to the ability to have resilience
cues.zh: 这些做法将使你的系统

cues.en: in those systems at operations time.
cues.zh: 在运行阶段具备韧性。

cues.en: The first is the support for continuous maintenance. I think the idea of doing maintenance on systems is completely
cues.zh: 首先是支持持续维护。我认为对系统进行维护这种想法，被完全

cues.en: misstated or misrepresented
cues.zh: 错误地表述或歪曲了

cues.en: as this sort of periodic or interval activity.
cues.zh: 变成了一种周期性或间歇性的活动。

cues.en: I think if you actually look at the systems that are under your partial control or under your management, you'll find that they are constantly being maintained
cues.zh: 我想如果你审视那些在你部分控制或管理下的系统，你会发现它们一直在进行各种形式的

cues.en: in some way. And I mean by this software maintenance, hardware maintenance,
cues.zh: 维护。我这里指的是软件维护、硬件维护、

cues.en: personnel kinds of activities,
cues.zh: 人员相关活动、

cues.en: physical plant maintenance, a whole variety of things. And I think that we have to design systems in which maintenance activities have now become so much a part of the system that they are actually part of the design of it, rather than something that we add on later using RPM code or something like that.
cues.zh: 物理设施维护以及各种各样的事情。我认为我们必须设计这样一种系统：其中的维护活动已深深融入系统，甚至成为系统设计的一部分，而不是后来通过 RPM 代码之类的方式附加上去的东西。

cues.en: I think we have to start
cues.zh: 我认为我们必须开始

cues.en: revealing
cues.zh: 向操作人员

cues.en: the controls to these systems to the operators.
cues.zh: 公开这些系统的控制接口。

cues.en: When it's 03:00 in the morning, the only people who are going to be able to help you are the operators and the control
cues.zh: 当时间来到凌晨三点，唯一能帮到你的人，就是坐在实际控制你系统的屏幕前的主操和

cues.en: people who are sitting in front of the screens that actually control your system.
cues.zh: 控制人员。

cues.en: And the way to make them able to deal with problems is to reveal the actual controls that are available there.
cues.zh: 而要让他们能够处理问题，办法就是公开那里实际可用的控制手段。

cues.en: I think it's absolutely essential that we recognize that the strength of the operator community is such that we must trust them with the controls to our systems.
cues.zh: 我认为，至关重要的是，我们要认识到运维社区的实力足够强，因此必须把系统的控制权托付给他们。

cues.en: This sounds a little bit subversive
cues.zh: 这听起来有点颠覆意味

cues.en: because many of you as you design systems are actually involved in trying to make it impossible for people to do things.
cues.zh: 因为你们中很多人在设计系统时，实际上是在努力让人们无法做某些事。

cues.en: You're trying to protect your systems from people doing things, but in fact I think that when we look at resilience and we make resilience our goal, we recognize that what we have to do is we have to develop some way of trusting people
cues.zh: 你们想保护系统，不让人们做这做那；但事实上，我认为当我们关注韧性、把韧性作为目标时，就会认识到，我们必须想出某种信任人的办法

cues.en: because we need them to act in situations where they're the only ones who are going to be able to do so, and therefore we have to actually reveal and expose the controls of our systems rather than trying to hide them away.
cues.zh: 因为我们需要他们在只有他们才能行动的情况下采取行动，因此我们必须真正揭示并公开系统的控制手段，而不是试图把它们藏起来。

cues.en: I think we have to show the lift points. Any of you who've gone around, worked around any heavy machinery or anything like that recognize that when heavy machinery is moved it's dangerous and hard, and so almost all heavy machinery has markers on it that shows where to lift it.
cues.zh: 我认为我们必须标出起吊点。你们中任何接触过、操作过重型机械之类的人都会明白，移动重型机械既危险又困难，所以几乎所有重型机械上都有标记，标明该从哪里起吊。

cues.en: We do that because we know it's going to get moved.
cues.zh: 我们这样做，是因为我们知道它迟早要被移动。

cues.en: We have to start building systems that show the lift points in the system itself. Where can I pick it up and move it? How could I actually take it and move it outside of the current system that I have and replace it with something else? And I think we don't do that very well in code, we don't do it very well in structures,
cues.zh: 我们必须开始构建能在系统自身中标出起吊点的系统。我能在哪里把它抬起来并移走？我怎样才能真正把它拿出来，移到我当前系统之外，并用别的东西替换它？我认为我们在代码里做得不好，在结构上做得也不好，

cues.en: and we certainly don't do it very well in our organizational stuff. Most of planning
cues.zh: 而在组织层面，我们当然也做得不好。大多数规划

cues.en: for maintenance is done at a kind of microscopic level that
cues.zh: 维护工作的大多数规划都是在一种微观层面上完成的，这种层面

cues.en: has no awareness of the kinds of things that can really happen.
cues.zh: 根本不了解真正可能发生的那类事情。

cues.en: I think we have to support mental simulation,
cues.zh: 我觉得我们必须支持心理模拟，

cues.en: and this means having people have clear ideas about how the system is actually configured and running.
cues.zh: 这意味着要让大家对系统的实际配置和运行方式有清晰的认识。

cues.en: You need to be able to have operators
cues.zh: 你需要让运维人员

cues.en: and the people who are working in your operations world be able to mentally simulate
cues.zh: 以及从事运维工作的人能够进行心理模拟，

cues.en: what is going to happen if they take some action, which means that they need to have access to deep knowledge of the system and its current status
cues.zh: 推演他们采取某些操作后会发生什么，这意味着他们需要深入了解系统及其当前状态，

cues.en: and it also means that you as the designers of those worlds have to present that information to operators so that they can see what's going on. You have to actually think about the kinds of situations that operators are going to confront and the kinds of work that they're going to do and you have to support the mental simulation that they're going to do as they're trying to figure out how to make the system work or recover.
cues.zh: 这也意味着你们作为这些系统的设计者，必须向运维人员呈现这些信息，让他们能够看清状况。你们必须切实思考运维人员将要面对的各种情况以及他们将要开展的工作，并且必须支持他们在试图弄清楚如何让系统运转或恢复时所进行的心理模拟。

cues.en: I think you have to open the objects and open your methods, I think that this idea about hiding in layers
cues.zh: 我认为你们必须公开对象和方法，我认为这种通过层层抽象

cues.en: of abstraction,
cues.zh: 来隐藏

cues.en: everything about the details is
cues.zh: 所有细节的想法，

cues.en: in fact pretty much run its course now. I think the idea that we can make these sort of black box devices
cues.zh: 其实现在已经差不多过时了。我认为那种我们可以制造出只了解其外壳而对内部运作一无所知的黑盒设备的想法，

cues.en: that we only know about the shell of and have no knowledge of the internal workings of is in fact a deep mistake.
cues.zh: 实际上是一个严重的错误。

cues.en: Because it turns out that in order to be able to make and reason about how the system is actually working,
cues.zh: 因为事实证明，为了能够构建系统并推断其真实运作方式，

cues.en: we have to have knowledge about what's inside the black box.
cues.zh: 我们必须掌握黑盒内部的情况。

cues.en: What's the hardest thing to do
cues.zh: 买一台新 PC 后，最难做的是什么

cues.en: when you buy
cues.zh: 当你买了

cues.en: a new PC?
cues.zh: 一台新 PC？

cues.en: What's the hardest part of the setup?
cues.zh: 安装过程中最难的部分是什么？

cues.en: Getting the wireless working,
cues.zh: 让无线网络正常工作，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: Because you bought the PC and you've got this wireless card and you're doing this thing, you're trying to get it going, should I use the Windows version or should I use the manufacturer's
cues.zh: 因为你买了 PC，装上了无线网卡，现在要让它运行起来：我该用 Windows 版本，还是制造商提供的

cues.en: version, I have two versions.
cues.zh: 版本？我这里有两个版本。

cues.en: Where should I set this parameter to this, should I set this parameter to that?
cues.zh: 这个参数该设成这样，还是该设成那样？

cues.en: No. The problem here is that you must be able to get off and see inside these layers.
cues.zh: 不。问题在于，你必须能够跳出来，看清这些层的内部。

cues.en: I think we have to deep six the don't touch me's, we have to get rid of this idea that there are parts of the system that cannot be operated and where we can't go, and I think we have to empower the operator learning.
cues.zh: 我认为我们必须彻底抛弃那些“禁止触碰”的部分，摒弃系统中有些部分无法操作、我们也无法进入的想法，还要赋能运维人员不断学习。

cues.en: What's the resilience agenda? I think there's operations I think the first agenda item for me is to convince you that operations are competent to hold the keys to the systems you build.
cues.zh: 什么是弹性议程？我认为这和运维有关。对我来说，第一项议程是让你相信，运维人员有能力掌管你所构建系统的控制权。

cues.en: That you should be willing to turn over the keys of your systems to your operations people. And if you don't have that confidence in them, you must do that, you must develop that. The second is that you've got to make resilience engineering the first priority for the design of your next generation systems,
cues.zh: 你应该愿意把系统的控制权交给运维人员。如果你对他们没有信心，就必须建立起这种信心。第二，你必须把弹性工程作为下一代系统设计的首要任务，

cues.en: and finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: you have to commit the resources to discovering, understanding, and supporting resilience throughout your component lifecycle.
cues.zh: 你必须投入资源，在整个组件生命周期中发现、理解并支持系统弹性。

cues.en: There's a bunch of stuff out there that you can look at. There's some papers by myself and my colleagues. There's some books on resilience engineering. If you search on the terms resilience engineering in quotes and the name Holnagle, you'll get all this stuff. If you go to my site,
cues.zh: 外面有很多资料可以看。有一些我和同事写的论文。还有一些关于弹性工程的书。如果你搜索带引号的“弹性工程”加上Holnagle这个名字，就能找到这些东西。如果你去我的网站，

cues.en: www.ctlab,
cues.zh: www.ctlab，

cues.en: there's a couple of papers out there that would be useful to you.
cues.zh: 上面有几篇论文对你会很有用。

cues.en: My time's up, thank you very much. And whatever you do,
cues.zh: 时间到了，非常感谢。还有，无论你做什么，

cues.en: don't visit me in my office.
cues.zh: 都别来办公室找我。
